title: This Beetle Runs So Fast It Goes Blind (125 Body Lengths a Second)

scenes.text: This beetle runs so fast it goes blind.
The tiger beetle covers 125 body lengths a second. For you, that's 480 miles an hour.
At that speed its eyes can't catch enough light. The world turns into a smear.
So it hunts in bursts: sprint, stop, find the prey again, sprint. It still wins.
It holds its antennae out front like a cane. Cut them off and it slams into things.
The fastest runner on Earth for its size can't see where it's going. It eats anyway.

description:
Tiger beetles run at up to about 125 body lengths a second, so fast their eyes cannot gather enough light to form an image and they go temporarily blind.
Cornell entomologists found the beetles hunt in a stop-and-go pattern, pausing three or four times to relocate prey, and hold their antennae rigid in front of them to feel obstacles. A human running at the same relative speed would be moving at roughly 480 miles an hour.
Which is the stranger superpower: running blind or kicking a rattlesnake in mid-air?
first_comment: The sprint record holder, an Australian tiger beetle, hits 2.5 metres a second with a body only 2 centimetres long. What would you do with a speed like that for one day?
